label: first input step, when the first token is one of b c d e h q r u v x 1 2 3
explanation: Fires only during the original-input phase. About two thirds of activations and of activation mass come at t=0. There it is fully determined by the first token: it fires every time that token is in {b,c,d,e,h,q,r,u,v,x,1,2,3} and never for any other token. Magnitude at t=0 depends on the token: 3 and c are highest (about 0.4-0.5 of max), b, h, q and r lowest. The other third of activations falls mostly at t=4-6 (a little at t=3 and t=7-8), on inputs from the same token set that are almost always first occurrences. This includes the strongest activations, e.g. 3 at t=5 after 2 at t=0, which reaches the max. But only about 15-20% of such steps fire, and I could not find a context rule for which ones do (checked: to_go, number of earlier set tokens). It never fires at t=1-2 or at t>=9, essentially never on the delimiter (once in the dev split), and never during the copy phase. The predicate covers only the deterministic t=0 component.
